title: Learn a reward from segment preferences
brief: Score trajectory segments with a learned reward, fit it with the Bradley-Terry loss on simulated preferences, check that the policy it induces matches the true one, and pick the next query by ensemble disagreement.
hints: segment_return sums the rewards. A mean makes a long segment of small rewards look worse than a short one, and a shift of every reward then changes which segment wins.

With z = (X[segs_a].sum(axis=1) - X[segs_b].sum(axis=1)) @ w, the loss for one pair is log(1 + exp(z)) - label * z, and its gradient is (sigmoid(z) - label) * (the feature-sum difference). Use np.logaddexp for the loss.
label 1 means A was preferred. If your fitted reward points the wrong way, check the sign of the label term first.
disagreement_query: probs = sigmoid(ws @ d.T) has shape (K, N), where d is the feature-sum difference per pair. Take the variance over axis 0 and argmax over the pairs.
